import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Signed digit sums in bases $b \ge 5$

The sequence is defined by
$$a(n) = \sum_{k=1}^n (-1)^{\operatorname{isprime}(k)} 10^k$$
where the sign is $-1$ if $k$ is prime, and $1$ if $k$ is not prime.

Generalizing the digit pattern observed in $a(n)$, it was conjectured on the OEIS entry that
for any base $b \ge 5$ and any choice of signs $\pm 1$, the absolute value of $\sum_{k=1}^n \pm b^k$
only contains digits in $\{0, 1, b-2, b-1\}$.

*References:*
- [A243106](https://oeis.org/A243106)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA243106


open Finset

/--
The sequence
$$a(n) = \sum_{k=1}^n (-1)^{\operatorname{isprime}(k)} 10^k$$
where the sign is $-1$ if $k$ is prime, and $1$ if $k$ is not prime.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : Int :=
  (Icc 1 n).sum fun k : ℕ =>
    (if Nat.Prime k then (-1 : Int) else 1) * (10 : Int) ^ k


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 10 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = -90 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = -1090 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 8910 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = -91090 := by rfl


/--
Conjecture: When expressed in base $b \ge 5$, the absolute value of any partial sum $\sum \pm b^k$ only contains digits belonging to $\{0, 1, b-2, b-1\}$.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/243106.wip.lean#L140"]
theorem digits_sum_restricted (b n : ℕ) (hb : b ≥ 5) :
    ∀ (σ : ℕ → Int) (hσ : ∀ k ∈ Icc 1 n, σ k = 1 ∨ σ k = -1),
      let x : Int := (Icc 1 n).sum fun k ↦ σ k * (b : Int) ^ k;
      ∀ d ∈ (b.digits x.natAbs), d = 0 ∨ d = 1 ∨ d = b - 2 ∨ d = b - 1 := by
    sorry

end OeisA243106

review.notes: Checked all seven declarations: OeisA243106.a, a_1–a_5, and digits_sum_restricted. The OEIS entry explicitly allows arbitrary signs on the first n positive powers, excluding exponent zero, and gives the same allowed digits. Its official mirror was used because the main entry returned a Cloudflare challenge. The definition and all five tests match the source; evaluated terms through n=19 also agree. Int.natAbs correctly handles negative sums, and b ≥ 5 excludes degenerate digit bases and truncated-subtraction issues. The n=0 case is harmless; Cano's additional information explicitly sets a(0)=0. Exhaustive Lean evaluations passed for every sign assignment with 0 ≤ n ≤ 10 and bases 5–16. The solved status agrees with the OEIS proof announcement dated May 26, 2026. The OEIS-linked AlphaProof Nexus proof has the identical target statement and was kernel-checked in /workspace/review/proofcheck.lean after updating an import path and one renamed integer-division lemma; its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
